stem: It is ironic that the scientist’s work was criticized recently for its ____ research methodology, since other researchers have argued for years that this same methodology was based absolutely on impeccable logic.

For private fossil collectors, a fossil’s value is (i)____ the object itself. For scientists, however, the value of a fossil is usually (ii)____. Most paleontological research focuses not only on the fossil itself, but also on the fossil’s location, the kind of rock it was found in, its position in the historical sequence, and how the fossil is positioned relative to other fossils.

Arguments based on mere possibilities (i)____ the difficulty of discussing future technology, not least since they (ii)____ public debates on technological options. A mere possibility argument such as “Agricultural biotechnology can have serious effects on ecosystems that we still know nothing about” can be taken by opponents of the technology to be (iii)____ whereas proponents tend to dismiss it completely.
colsZh: 代表，体现，是…的典型范例

stem: Ruth Carter's campaigns for Congress were pretty ____: as a liberal in a deeply conservative district, she was virtually certain to lose.
optsZh: 不合乎礼节的，不得体的

stem: To most ethicists, self-interested action connotes the opposite of moral conduct, and its ____ is for them a virtual prerequisite for serious ethical discourse.

The recognition of ____ the movements of the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars gave many ancient societies the ability to project the past into the future, lending a predictability to the variable cosmos.

The professional curator in Native American tribal museums ideally serves as ____, using her museological training to design exhibits that effectively convey to museumgoers the messages that the tribal community chooses to disseminate.
